content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or mixed (especially after recent spikes).  
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment is strongly negative and recent prices are trending down.  
- Overshoot after positive sentiment spikes — model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high relative to recent 18-day average when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Lagged corrections: model delays downward adjustments when sentiment turns negative — true price drops faster than forecasted.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is consistently negative over last 18 days.  
- Avoid extrapolating recent upward momentum into 30-day forecast if sentiment turns negative — true price often reverses within 5–7 days.
